gaps_to_exploit: The head term is contested between (a) a lender's commercial vendor page (PT SMI), (b) a substantially DATED government explainer still quoting 2015-2019 RPJMN numbers, (c) a bare directory of scheme names with no explanation, and (d) academic PDFs. NO ONE owns a current, practitioner-grade, decision-useful national explainer.

Nobody reconciles the funding-gap figures. Sources circulate US$625.37bn / Rp10.303tn / Rp10.146tn / US$625bn need and US$375bn vs US$377.2bn gap, and APBD at US$104.31bn vs US$106.31bn — with scope and base year rarely stated. A section that teaches readers how to read these numbers is high-trust, on-brand for the reference-year discipline, and unmatched on the SERP.
The three financing routes (government financing / corporate financing / project financing) are NAMED across the corpus but never turned into a decision framework with thresholds.
Lender-side diligence is described only in one short Kemenkeu Q&A. No page walks a sponsor through what a credit committee actually tests, or what raises cost of fund.
No competing page includes an honest 'when this does NOT work' section — the strongest available differentiator per style_guide 1a.
Nothing in the corpus carries a comparison table a decision-maker would screenshot and forward.
